key_insight: Y6 excitons are hybrid Frenkel–charge-transfer states with 20–40% charge-transfer character, enabling delocalization-assisted transport and rapid interfacial quenching.
engineering_relevance: These parameters give device designers a quantitative handle on how Y6 film morphology and interfaces control charge injection and exciton harvesting in single-component solar cells.
method: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy measured exciton quenching in Y6 films near hole-transport interfaces.
An analytical hybrid Frenkel–charge-transfer model extracted intermolecular coupling, charge-transfer fraction, and system-bath interaction strengths.
The model links spectroscopic signals to microscopic transport mechanisms without relying only on phenomenological diffusion fits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~1 ps quenching within ~4 nm of the interface, supporting a short-range injection mechanism enabled by exciton delocalization.
watch_item: The extracted transport picture is model-dependent and may vary with film morphology, interface chemistry, and whether the same parameters transfer to other non-fullerene acceptors.
paper_title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells
